data.name: Hadassina
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Hadassah means myrtle tree. Myrtle was a symbol of royalty and beauty in ancient Israel. The prophet Isaiah wrote, 'The Lord will create over all the earth one new man, and they shall all dwell safely. And a new moon shall be great over the house of David, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem shall rejoice, and give gladness, and joy, and corn, and wine, and oil, and milk, and honey, and a soul shall be saved, for the seed of Judah, and a child shall be born for this city; and the days of her mourning shall be ended, because the desolation is departed from her, and she shall be called Myrtle Tree, and the place thereof Shame out of the Lord; for the Lord hath chosen Zion, and will sanctify it; this shall be her name for evermore.', which refers to the rebirth and restoration of Jerusalem, represented by the myrtle tree.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the beauty, joy, and hope that comes with new beginnings.

in_hebrew.name: הדסינה
in_hebrew.meaning: עץ הדס, סמל של חברות ואהבה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם הדסינה מקורו בעברית ומייצג את העץ הדס, שהיה סמל של חברות ואהבה. בבית המקדש, הדסים היו ניטעים באזור הכותל המערבי. העץ גם ייצג את אהבת האלוהים, כפי שהוזכר בספר שיר השירים (1:14).

in_greek.name: Χαδασσίνα
in_greek.meaning: βλάστημα του δαφνός, σύμβολο της αγάπης
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χαδασσίνα προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη για τη δάφνη, με τη δάφνη να συμβολίζει την αγάπη. Στον Ιουδαϊσμό, η δάφνη ήταν ένα σύμβολο της αιώνιας αγάπης του Θεού. Στον Χριστιανισμό, η δάφνη απεικονίζει την αγάπη και την ειλικρίνεια, όπως αναφέρεται στο Ευαγγέλιο του Λουκά (10:27).

in_latin.name: Hadassina
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Hadassina a radice Hebraica derivatur, significans flos carni, id est caritas. In Ecclesia primitiva, flos carni erat symbolus amoris, quem Deus habet erga hominem. In traditione Christiana, flos carni repraesentat dilectio et sinceritas, ut in Evangelio secundum Lucam (10,27) scriptum est.

In the Christian tradition, the myrtle flower represents love, friendship, and devotion, as seen in the book of Proverbs (31:10).

The name can also represent a connection to the rich history and cultural heritage of the Jewish people.

It can also serve as a symbol of faithfulness, as myrtle trees are known for their long-lasting and enduring nature. Additionally, the name can be a source of comfort and hope, as it points towards the ultimate restoration and redemption of God's creation.

She was taken to the harem of the king, renamed Esther, and eventually saved her people by revealing her Jewish identity to the king and exposing the plot of Haman to destroy them.

Hadassah, a prophetess, played a significant role in the early Christian community. She was known for her wisdom and prophecies. According to tradition, she lived around the time of Christ and was instrumental in the conversion of the Roman centurion Longinus to Christianity.
